RVG29 can be used as a targeting ligand for gene delivery across the blood-brain barrier.
the RVG29 modified NPs are able to cross the BBB through specific cellular uptake and the BBB-crossing efficiency can be enhanced by the RVG29 modification.
the RVG29 peptide can efficiently deliver genes across the BBB, which can be used as a novel strategy for the gene therapy for neurological diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the RVG29 peptide can be modified on the PAMAM/DNAs to form NPs, which are able to be taken by the BCECs via a specific receptor-mediated endocytosis, and the BBB-crossing efficiency and brain targeting efficiency can be significantly improved.

RVG29 is a promising brain targeting ligand and the PEGylation of dendrimers could improve the cellular uptake and BBB permeability of the NPs, which may be of potential value in the treatment of central nervous system disorders.
